488b29: Common to all animals are the parts by which it receives the
488b30: food and that into which it receives it; and these are both the same and different
488b31: in the ways already stated, either in form or in degree of excess or
488b34: by which it discharges the residue of the food [and by which it takes it in]; for
489a1: not all animals possess this. That by which it takes in food is called
489a2: the mouth, and that into which it receives it, the stomach; the remaining part has many names.
489a4: parts for the liquid residue, it also has them for the dry food,
489a5: but those that have the latter do not all have the former. Hence all that have a bladder
489a6: also have a stomach, but those that have a stomach do not all have a bladder.
